candidate.scope: The DP-Seq (Designed Primer-based RNA-sequencing, DP-seq) row of the assigned Illumina poster: primer definition plus poly(A)-selected RNA → first-strand cDNA → designed-primer hybridization → amplified DNA. Neighboring Quartz-Seq and Smart-seq/NanoCAGE/CAGEscan rows and the right-hand chemistry panel are outside the DP-Seq target. operations.label: Define set of heptamer primers

operations.information_effect: Reference-sequence information determines which cDNA regions can be preferentially amplified and potentially assigned to transcripts; unique-sequence design does not make every product uniquely assignable. operations.label: Hybridize primers
operations.description: Anneal the physical designed-primer reagents to complementary positions on first-strand cDNA, yielding primed templates. s_primer_design is a specification input identifying these reagents; it is not an additional molecule in the reaction.
operations.mechanism: The heptamer target-binding portions pair with the cDNA; the primary paper describes these as partially hybridized primers because of their universal tails.
operations.information_effect: Primer binding selects local regions for copying; secondary structure and mispriming affect which regions are represented, so hybridization does not prove perfect target specificity.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports acceptance at the declared DP-Seq schematic scope. All eight states, five local operations, twelve connections, the single method scope, its listed primary reference, and both interpretation records were checked individually. The design branch and the complete poly(A)-RNA → cDNA → primer-bound cDNA → DNA route are retained. The hybridization interface jointly combines template and primer reagents, with a separate specification input; no independent sample branches are collapsed. RNA is the biological source, cDNA and amplicons carry its selected sequence information, and the depicted endpoint precedes sequencing-adaptor preparation. No consequential unsupported claim, omitted depicted transformation, or unresolved applicability remains.
